claims: 1. A method, comprising: attaching a silane or a silane derivative to a surface of a patterned substrate including a flow channel having depressions defined therein, wherein the depressions are separated by interstitial regions, thereby forming silanized depressions and silanized interstitial regions; applying a functionalized coating layer in the silanized depressions and on the silanized interstitial regions; polishing the functionalized coating layer from the silanized interstitial regions; grafting a primer to the functionalized coating layer in the silanized depressions to form a grafted functionalized coating layer in the depressions; and applying a hydrogel on the grafted functionalized coating layer in the depressions.
2. The method as defined in claim 1, wherein applying the hydrogel involves applying an aqueous mixture including from about 0.001% up to about 0.1% (mass to volume) of a hydrogel material.

3. The method as defined in claim 1 or 2, wherein the hydrogel material is selected from the group consisting of a poly(N-(5-azidoacetamidylpentyl) acrylamide-co-acrylamide), crosslinked polyacrylamide, an agarose gel, and crosslinked polyethylene glycol.

4. The method as defined in any of claims 1 through 3, wherein: a spacer layer is bonded to the patterned substrate and defines a perimeter of the flow channel; and after the hydrogel is applied, the method further comprises bonding a lid to the spacer layer.

5. The method as defined in any of claims1 through 4, wherein after the functionalized coating layer is polished and before the primer is grafted, the method further comprises bonding a lid to at least some of the interstitial regions.
6. The method as defined in any of claims1 through 5, wherein applying the hydrogel includes selectively depositing the hydrogel on the grafted functionalized coating layer in the depressions.

claims: 1. A multilayer article, comprising: (i) a polymeric substrate comprising extractable atoms; and (ii) a hydrogel coating thereon, wherein the hydrogel coating has a water content of at least 10 wt.% and is covalently bonded to the polymeric substrate, and wherein the hydrogel coating is derived from an aqueous composition having a pH of less than 9.5, the aqueous composition comprising: (a) a hydrophilic monomer selected from at least one of (meth) acrylate or (meth) acrylamide; (b) at least 0.1 wt% water swellable clay; (c) a first initiator, wherein the first initiator is water soluble and is a type I photoinitiator; and (d) a second initiator, wherein the second initiator is water soluble and is a type II photoinitiator; and (e) and (4) acid.
2. The multilayer article of claim 1, wherein the polymeric substrate comprises at least one of polyurethane, polyamide, polyester, and polypropylene.
3. The multilayer article of claim 1, wherein the polymeric substrate is free of a primer.

4. The multilayer article of claim 1, wherein the first initiator is 2-hydroxy-4' - (2-hydroxyethoxy) -2-methylpropiophenone, and the second initiator comprises at least one of 4- (3-sulfopropoxy) benzophenone, 2- (3-sulfopropoxy) thioxanthen-9-one, carboxybenzophenone, and salts thereof.
5. The multilayer article of claim 1, wherein the aqueous composition comprises less than 5% alcohol relative to the weight of the aqueous composition.
6. The multilayer article of claim 1 wherein the aqueous composition has a pH of less than 8.
7. The multilayer article of claim 1, wherein the hydrogel coating has a thickness of at least 0.1 mm.

8. The multilayer article of claim 1, wherein the hydrogel coating further comprises an additive selected from at least one of polyethylene glycol, polyethylene glycol-co-polypropylene oxide copolymers, partially hydrolyzed polyvinyl acetate, polyvinylpyrrolidone, glycerol or glycerol derivatives, methylcellulose or other cellulose derivatives, polyoxazolines, and natural gums.
9. The multilayer article of claim 1, wherein the multilayer article is a wound dressing.

10. A method of making a hydrogel coated article, the method comprising: (i) providing an aqueous composition having a pH of less than 9.5, the aqueous composition comprising: (a) a hydrophilic monomer selected from at least one of (meth) acrylate or (meth) acrylamide; (b) at least 0.1 wt% water swellable clay; (c) a first initiator, wherein the first initiator is water soluble and is a type I photoinitiator; (d) a second initiator, wherein the second initiator is water soluble and is a type II photoinitiator; and (e) an acid; (ii) contacting the aqueous composition with a polymeric substrate comprising extractable atoms; and (iii) curing the aqueous composition.
